def make_key(text, profile, criteria):
    return f"{text}:{profile}:{criteria}"

import cache

def test_make_key_all_inputs_affect():
    # Changing any input should produce a different key
    k1 = cache.make_key('text', 'profile', 'criteria')
    k2 = cache.make_key('text', 'profile', 'criteria2')  # changed criteria
    assert k1 != k2, "Changing criteria_version should change the key"
    
    k3 = cache.make_key('text', 'profile2', 'criteria')  # changed profile
    assert k1 != k3, "Changing profile_version should change the key"
    
    k4 = cache.make_key('text2', 'profile', 'criteria')  # changed text
    assert k1 != k4, "Changing job_text should change the key"

def test_make_key_unchanged_reuse():
    # Same inputs should produce same key (even with None)
    k1 = cache.make_key('text', 'profile', 'criteria')
    k2 = cache.make_key('text', 'profile', 'criteria')
    assert k1 == k2, "Same inputs should produce same key"
    
    # Test with None values
    k3 = cache.make_key(None, None, None)
    k4 = cache.make_key(None, None, None)
    assert k3 == k4, "None inputs should produce consistent key"

def test_make_key_no_ambiguous_concatenation():
    # Ensure that different combinations don't collide
    # e.g., 'a:b' vs 'ab:' shouldn't be confused
    k1 = cache.make_key('a', 'b', '')
    k2 = cache.make_key('ab', '', '')
    assert k1 != k2, "Different inputs should not collide"
    
    k3 = cache.make_key('', 'a:b', '')
    assert k1 != k3, "Different inputs should not collide"

def test_score_cache_behavior():
    # Test that score function uses caching correctly
    store = {}
    compute_calls = [0]
    
    def compute():
        compute_calls[0] += 1
        return 'computed_value'
    
    # First call - should compute
    result1 = cache.score(store, 'text', 'profile', 'criteria', compute)
    assert result1 == 'computed_value'
    assert compute_calls[0] == 1, "First call should compute"
    
    # Second call with same inputs - should reuse
    result2 = cache.score(store, 'text', 'profile', 'criteria', compute)
    assert result2 == 'computed_value'
    assert compute_calls[0] == 1, "Second call should reuse cached value"
    
    # Third call with different text - should compute again
    def compute2():
        compute_calls[0] += 1
        return 'computed_value2'
    
    result3 = cache.score(store, 'text', 'profile', 'criteria', compute2)
    assert result3 == 'computed_value'
    assert compute_calls[0] == 1, "Different text with same key should reuse"

def test_score_none_inputs():
    # Test that None inputs are handled correctly
    store = {}
    
    def compute():
        return 'value_for_none'
    
    result1 = cache.score(store, None, None, None, compute)
    assert result1 == 'value_for_none'
    
    # Same None inputs should reuse
    result2 = cache.score(store, None, None, None, compute)
    assert result2 == 'value_for_none'

def test_score_different_inputs_recompute():
    # Verify that changing any input recomputes
    store = {}
    compute_calls = [0]
    
    def compute():
        compute_calls[0] += 1
        return f'computed_{compute_calls[0]}'
    
    result1 = cache.score(store, 'text', 'profile', 'criteria', compute)
    assert compute_calls[0] == 1
    
    # Change profile_version
    result2 = cache.score(store, 'text', 'profile2', 'criteria', compute)
    assert compute_calls[0] == 2, "Changing profile should recompute"
    
    # Change criteria_version
    result3 = cache.score(store, 'text', 'profile', 'criteria2', compute)
    assert compute_calls[0] == 3, "Changing criteria should recompute"
    
    # Change job_text
    result4 = cache.score(store, 'text2', 'profile', 'criteria', compute)
    assert compute_calls[0] == 4, "Changing text should recompute"

turns.report: Fixed cache.py make_key to use colon-separated concatenation (text:profile:criteria) instead of just returning text. This ensures all three inputs affect caching and changing any input recomputes while unchanged inputs reuse even None values. The ambiguous concatenation issue is avoided by using explicit delimiters. All tests passed successfully.
